elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.8 permits the Customer to terminate its participation in the Agreement for convenience, providing the operative agreement-level exit appropriate to this multiparty agreement.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.8 requires not less than thirty days' prior written notice, so Customer can exercise the right on 30 days' written notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.8 requires the other Parties to refund, pro rata, all Customer-prepaid amounts attributable to the period after termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Only Customer receives the added unilateral mid-term convenience right. Under Subparagraphs 18.1 and 18.2, other Parties cannot terminate during the 25-year Initial Period absent unanimous written agreement.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate on 30 days' notice, rather than notice within the required 60-to-90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed for Customer's Subparagraph 18.8 termination; instead, Customer receives a pro-rata refund. The conditional cap is therefore unnecessary.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1 permits any Party to terminate at the end of the Initial Period or at any time thereafter, so post-Initial-Period termination is not restricted to a term-end date.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Subparagraph 18.1 requires any terminating Party to give at least one year's prior written notice, exceeding 90 days.
